triage.author: Carolyn J
triage.title: The Arrogance of AI
triage.text: The building’s architecture is stunning, modern and congruent with its prairie setting.  But we were not prepared for the Disney-meets-Instagram experience inside.  One is routed through rooms that depict in banal terms the major events of TR’s life in a way that assumes all humans react in the same predictable way: the dark room with only his diary page on a sad day, the 20 foot cartoons of forest animals depicting a childhood day, the 35 ft concave wall blasting his speech in endless loop - in case one is too dull to get it the first time — and the holographic animation that we watched actual, live adults introduce themselves to it and converse.  Ridiculous.  Compared to FDR’s dignified and substantive collection at Hyde Park, it is a picture book compared to an encyclopedia.  In AI think, we are all just subjects to be manipulated in predictable ways.

triage.author: Alyssa Mitchell
triage.text: This museum has so much potential. A lot of the exhibits are beautiful and tell the story of his life. HOWEVER. The use of generative AI slop is appalling, and the antithesis of what TR stood for. I teared up watching the segment on his work with national parks and public lands, knowing the threats they face from this current administration allowing the growth of AI data centers, amongst other setbacks in federal protections. Truly shameful, do better. There’s such an easy way to make this so much better.

triage.author: Benjamin Scott
triage.text: Drove hours out of my way to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora—because let’s be real, there’s not much else pulling people through that stretch of North Dakota. Got turned away at the door for not having a timed ticket. Explained the long drive, asked if there was any way to work with us, and the staff member looked almost insulted that I’d even asked. I’ve visited presidential libraries and the Smithsonian on the Fourth of July without this nonsense. You’re not the Louvre out there, folks. A little North Dakota hospitality would’ve gone a long way.

triage.author: Den Mac
triage.text:
I have to keep reminding myself this place only opened in July. The concept is good and the place is beautiful. However, there are flow issues inside. There needs to be better signage to match the map for timeline accuracy visiting of the different areas.
While there are a lot of beautiful artifacts, the description placards contain too small of print & some of the placards have words worn off already.
In the gift shop, I think maybe they didn't plan to be so busy because they were sold out of some basic items such as TR Library stickers.

In the cafe, they could be more efficient if they would have a menu visible from the line instead of not until you get to the counter. Very beautiful grounds and conveniently located near the Medora Musical.

triage.author: cdb
triage.text:
We visited on a Sunday at the end of October.  The Library is a beautiful facility in a serene setting.  The exterior blends in splendidly with the natural landscape.

We arrived early and sat inside in comfy chairs by huge picture windows.  I bought postcards first thing while there was no one in the gift shop.  Items are spendy, the postcards were $2.99 each.  There was no price by the display and thanks to the clerk, she made sure I knew how much I was going to be charged.  When it was our appointed time to enter the exhibits, there was a throng of people getting their pictures taken at the AI photo stations. We bypassed that option and started our visit.

My overall impression was favorable, although there were several letdowns for me.
CROWD SIZE:  Having just opened in July, this attraction is drawing sizable crowds and every display had people standing side by side to view display items and it was not easy to walk between the exhibit cases.  I could tell a lot of thought went into all the exhibits, but I was only able to see a few items without reading the information.  My advice is to check the website and see when there are a lot of unreserved times - I think that would allow for more 'elbow room' and the ability to take in the displays.
We experienced several of the themed rooms and they were all in working order and still had a new feeling.  I enjoyed the room where Teddy answered questions.
THE RESTROOM:  This was a serious disappointment and worth revision consideration by the organization.  I cannot speak to the restroom configuration by the cafe, but the one in the exhibit area had to have been someone's minimalist brainchild.  The stalls were arranged in a small area and were unisex. I think there were four regular stalls and one ADA.  When I got into a stall, either the man before me or another user had peed on the seat.  My husband said the one he used was in the same shape.  The common sink area could accommodate two people comfortably while stall users moved out into the sink space.  I get the concept, but separate restrooms are the way to go.  I cannot remember if there would have been room to plumb a urinal in each of the stalls.
FINDING THE EXIT:  OMG, when we'd pegged out our fun meter and wanted to leave, we had a dickens of a time finding the exit.  I can honestly say when we finally saw the signage, it was small and up high.  I would be interested to know what the emergency exit strategy is when it might be necessary to move several hundred people out of a crowded area.  The map we received at the start of our visit was of no help.  We looked for a docent to get help, but could not locate one.
GOOD TO KNOW:  I use walking poles for balance and had no problem with the ability to use them in this facility.  There was a water fountain with a water bottle filling station, so I assumed I could have brought my own water bottle.  People were wearing sling pouches/purses, so that would have been an option since the website specifically forbids backpacks.  Non-flash photography is fine.
DEFINITELY WORTH A SECOND VISIT:  I imagine as time goes by, visitation will relax and it will be easier to see what's on display inside the Library.  We'll give it a try again during the off season.  Personally we would avoid visiting in spring and summer.  We'll visit again in fall.

triage.author: Deb Johnson
triage.text: We loved this interactive museum and library.  Kids were having fun doing activities using the bracelet, as well as the adults.  Be sure to get a bracelet and have your photo taken or you will miss a lot.  The walkway outside is wonderful, but I did notify the museum that the steps on the boardwalk need to be marked on the edge.  We almost fell but noticed them at the last second. There is one very cute play area for little children inside, but most activities were for an older child or adult. We have been to many presidential libraries and this one was the best!

triage.author: sydney evans
triage.text:
An incredibly interactive presidential library experience-state of the art and appealing to all ages! Although the background of TRs life-what shaped him, rise to presidency was great, wish there had been a little more content on his presidential time. The take home pictures, mementos are a great way for guests to personalize their experiences. Creating motivation to follow in his footsteps is well done: empowerment as an individual to make a difference in the world.
The site of the library, architecture are phenomenal. Breathtaking views all around.
The gift shop-although there are some nice offerings-is overpriced. More variety needed perhaps.? Doesn’t need to be “kitschy” but more quality items. More TR specific related items vs high end expensive clothing..? Children’s beginners conservation kits-for bug/ butterflies..? Love the Robert Frost children’s books but a few more.
The cafe was ok-enjoyed my turkey meatloaf sandwich and my husband liked the bison “sloppy Joe”. After reading the chef’s background, maybe I had higher expectations. Also, if it had been busier, more seating, kiosks would definitely be needed. As it was, time of year-lots of elderly guests were the majority and seemed to be slow on kiosk operations, which made line, wait time a little long.
I know this beautiful library has only been open a few months and kinks will reveal themselves. I’d highly recommend anyone to visit this extraordinary presidential library-fabulous!
Medora is a quaint little town that will in time respond to guest needs/wants. The juxtaposition of the TR National Park is not to be missed. We had a marvelous time there too. I would recommend at least one nights stay to take it all in.

triage.author: Charles Bennett
triage.text:
The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library was nothing short of amazing.  I've been to only two others, Eisenhower, and Truman. They don't even come close.
Everything about was perfect. The flow the interactive things,  seating was everywhere,  flow was well planned and kids will not be bored.
My one and only complaint was when I asked the AI Roosevelt if he enjoyed the subermarine ride. He replied that he'd never been aboard a submarine.
In fact, he was actually the first president to ride and pilot a submarine and a placard in the main hall says so.
I recommend a visit. We loved everything and spent about two hours.  Very informative and easy to understand. You will learn, laugh, and cry.

7.headline: Ratings easing to 4.65 across 26 reviews
paragraphs: 26 reviews in the last 7 days, down 6 on the previous 7 days. The average is down 0.07. 7.7% rated three stars or below.

Visitors are consistently praising the interactive exhibits, the building and how well it works for families. The AI experience is the sharpest split in the feedback: it is the most praised feature in the building and the named reason for 2 low ratings in this window.

The complaints that cost us stars cluster tightly. The most frequent is the reaction against the AI experience (2 mentions). These are operational and messaging fixes rather than problems with the experience itself, which is the better problem to have. Separately, 11 reviews are waiting on a reply and 6 are past our own service level.

actions.issue: the reaction against the AI experience

notes: 20 reviews predate public opening, averaging 4.4. These are press, donor and Founding Member previews. They count toward all-time figures but are held out of the response queue.
